why: Each sprinkler is an interval [i - r, i + r] clipped to [0, n], and you need the fewest intervals covering [0, n]. That is greedy interval covering, which is the jump-game greedy once you record the farthest reach from each left end.
hints: Turn each sprinkler into the interval it waters. What is the question now?

Minimum intervals to cover a segment: from the covered frontier, among all intervals starting at or before it, choose the one reaching farthest. far[left] = the best right end among intervals starting at left.
Build far[] in O(n), then sweep like Jump Game II. Each layer extends the frontier to the farthest reach seen; if it cannot move, return -1. O(n) time and space.
pitfalls: Coverage is of a continuous segment: [0,1] and [2,3] leave the gap (1,2), so the next interval must start at or before the current end.
Clip intervals to [0, n] before indexing.
Return -1 if the frontier stalls before n.
